findings.title: Recreate the queue pool when a strategy is recreated
findings.body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and passes that same pool to every strategy. During a Kafka rebalance, Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates another through create_with_partitions; closing the old strategy shuts down this pool's queues and workers. The replacement strategy consequently submits to already-shutdown queues. Those submissions raise, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches the exceptions and marks the offsets complete, so results received after a rebalance can be committed without being processed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle tied to the individual strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

findings.title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
findings.body: Each queue is constructed without a maxsize, and submission always accepts more work without raising MessageRejected. If result processing is slower than Kafka consumption—or one worker is blocked—the consumer continues retaining decoded results, original Kafka messages, and offset-tracking entries indefinitely. Unlike the bounded batching path, this mode has no limit on outstanding work and can exhaust process memory under sustained load. Bound outstanding work and reject submissions until capacity becomes available.

findings.title: Drain accepted work and commit it before completing graceful shutdown
findings.body: close() stops the commit thread before shutting down workers, and pool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False). Workers therefore exit after their current item rather than draining accepted queued items; completions after the commit thread exits are never committed. In addition, worker.join(timeout=5.0) can return while a result processor is still running, and strategy.join() ignores its supplied timeout and simply calls close() again. During a rebalance this can leave an old worker modifying subscription state after a new partition owner starts processing replayed results, breaking per-subscription ordering. Graceful close/join must drain accepted work, wait for in-flight processing within the requested timeout, and commit the final completed offsets before returning.
